newsitem.title: USA: Natgas/oil in-kind royalties could work-U.S. MMS.
newsitem.headline: Natgas/oil in-kind royalties could work-U.S. MMS.

text.p: In-kind payments of federal natural gas royalties could increase government revenues and cut administrative costs, but a similar program for crude oil may not work as well, the director of the U.S. Minerals Management Service said Thursday.
"We are encouraged by the prospects for gas RIK from both revenue and administrative perspectives," MMS Director Cynthia Quarterman told a House Resources subcommittee.
But she said, "We are not convinced that crude oil RIK is in the best interests of the United States."
Quarterman said the findings of the MMS' study on using in-kind payments for royalties on oil and gas extracted from federal leases were preliminary.
But she said, "An overall finding of the study will likely be that, under favorable circumstances, RIK prorams could be workable, revenue neutral, or positive."

Quarterman warned however that a RIK system for onshore crude oil "would be large and complex because of the scattered nature of the production. This would make such a RIK program a difficult undertaking that should be attempted only if revenue and administrative impacts for all parties are decidedly positive."
While she said she was not convinced an oil royalty in-kind program would save money, she said the agency was willing to work with states, industry and the Congress on a pilot program.
